notes:
Account summary: mid-market product org (PLG + sales) building an AI-first search + agent layer across their product. Started on Hosted API (quick prototyping) — moved to Dedicated evaluation after perf tests and cost modeling.

Key ask: predictable unit economics for peak shopping periods. Team wants committed baseline for steady traffic + defined burst pool that can be used without manual approval. Concerned about overage pricing — request granular per-token or per-inference overage caps and transparent compute vs. model licensing splits.

POC history: used hosted_api with 3 models (base, tuned, reranker) for 6 weeks. Observed 22% token cost reduction with Redwood Optimize suggestions during POC (batching + KV cache). Decision to evaluate Dedicated driven by: predictable latency during high concurrency, VPC for data residency, and lower per-token unit cost at scale.

Pricing talk notes (from 2026-01-22 call):
- "We need a firm commit with burst that doesn't break the budget" — VP Product.
- Redwood proposed 3-tier commit ramp: 6-month ramp (40% year1 commit -> 70% year2), dedicated burst pool (10% of committed qps) with controlled overage price at 1.5x base, and 90-day price protection clause.
- Silvercrest pushback: wants max overage multiplier at 1.25x and option to convert burst usage into committed capacity mid-term with pro-rata billing.

Security/compliance: SOC2 is table stakes; they require SSO (SAML), KMS integration for key management, audit logs exported to their SIEM, and data residency for EU customers (multi-region routing). VPC private control plane is required for Dedicated.

Commercial constraints: procurement prefers fixed monthly commit vs annual prepay. Finance prefers ramped commit schedule aligned to expected ARR growth. They asked for 3 pricing scenarios: conservative (50% commit vs forecast), expected (75%), aggressive (100%) with differing discounts and burst allowances.

Quotes/attachments: Drive pricing deck v3 includes model-by-model PPS (per-prompt-second) proposals and examples of ramp schedules. Jira RDW-1129 tracks a technical blocker on encryption-at-rest key rotation process.

Rep notes — shorthand:
- Hosted POC strong: latency 90th pctl ~85ms on small model, ~220ms on tuned model during peak.
- Cost target: <$0.006 per 1k tokens equivalent at steady-state for primary support flow.
- They will sign if we accept: 12-month commit at 120k qps-seconds equivalent, burst pool 15% with convert option, overage cap 1.25x base, and SOW addendum for SLA.
- "Legal will want the SOW to explicitly call out fallback behavior if Dedicated capacity degraded" — SE.
